driftTypes.definition: A production surface or consumer resolves from a stale, unauthorized, candidate, or otherwise non-canonical source instead of the governed production source.
A production route diverges from its governed resolution, canonical source, locale, audience, cache, or redirect contract.
A public or production projection diverges from the canonical five-book, fifteen-part, volume, or publication-ownership architecture.
A governed asset is unresolved, missing, unconsumed, deprecated-but-consumed, or bypassed by an unauthorized hard-coded asset path.
A rendered composition diverges from governed CPR composition lineage, slot ownership, or WPR projection boundaries.
A production projection diverges from its governed locale identity, route-locale relationship, or locale-specific production source.
A production runtime declares an expected web surface or consumer but has no actual governed consumer, unless webProjection is explicitly NONE_BY_DESIGN.
Repository production state and live deployment evidence are stale, missing, or not aligned to the accepted deployment candidate.
A public surface leaks restricted internal vocabulary, stale method naming, old volume wording, incorrect book-volume naming, or internal codes.
A production surface falls below its governed visual coverage expectation or diverges from the accepted visual production projection.
PUBLIC, CUSTOMER, or PROFESSIONAL isolation diverges across cache, hydration, storage, response headers, indexing, data purpose, consent, or professional authorization.
